findings.title: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category is unset or invalid
findings.body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. Site settings rows only exist when a value has been changed from its default, so on any install where `embed_category` was never set (or was set to a value that doesn't match a category name, including the default empty string), the query returns zero rows and `[0]` is nil, making `[0]['id']` raise NoMethodError. The `category_id == 0` fallback on line 14 never gets a chance to run. This breaks `db:migrate` for the majority of existing sites. The code must handle an empty result (e.g. `result.first.try(:[], 'id').to_i`) before indexing.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are not normalized, so existing embeds silently break
findings.body: The migration inserts the raw strings from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting directly via SQL, bypassing the model's `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` prefixes and paths. The old setting explicitly accepted values like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` (the previous code and tests did `h.sub(/^https?\:\/\//, '')` when matching). After migration, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against the parsed URI host (`discourse.org`), so a stored value of `http://discourse.org` will never match and embedding will stop working for those hosts with no error shown to the admin. The migration should apply the same scheme/path stripping before inserting.

findings.title: SQL string interpolation of site setting values in INSERT
findings.body: The INSERT statement interpolates the raw host string `h` (read from the `site_settings.value` text column) directly into SQL: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. Any stored value containing a single quote (possible since the old setting was free-form text) will either break the migration with a SQL syntax error or produce a malformed row. Use `sanitize_sql`/quoted values or `EmbeddableHost.create!` instead of string interpolation.

findings.title: update and destroy raise NoMethodError (500) when the host id doesn't exist
findings.body: Both `update` (`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` then `save_host(host)` which calls `host.host = ...`) and `destroy` (`host.destroy`) operate on the result of a `.first` lookup without checking for nil. A request with a stale or invalid id (e.g. an admin UI with an out-of-date row, or a deleted record) produces `NoMethodError: undefined method ... for nil:NilClass` and a 500 error instead of a 404. Guard with `fail ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` or an equivalent not-found response.

findings.title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a silent no-op
findings.body: The `update` action is identical to `show`: it re-fetches and re-serializes the embedding object without reading or persisting any request parameters. Meanwhile the client controller wires `saveChanges` to `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which issues this PUT. Any caller of this endpoint gets a 200 success response while nothing is saved, which is a misleading API contract (and the `saveChanges` client action is dead/misleading UI code). Either implement persistence or remove the PUT route and the client action.

findings.title: before_validation raises on nil host instead of producing a validation error
findings.body: The `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. If the `host` attribute is nil (e.g. a create/update request where `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is missing, so the controller assigns nil), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` and returns a 500 error rather than a 422 validation failure. Guard with `if self.host.present?` and rely on `validates_format_of` (plus a presence validation) to reject blank hosts.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb
findings.body: After this change, `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` contains the `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` definition, while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `Fabricator(:category)`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` definitions. Because Fabrication loads all files in the directory the specs still pass, but the files are misnamed relative to their contents, which will confuse anyone editing category or embeddable-host fixtures later. The contents should live in the correctly named files.

findings.title: New admin controllers have no behavioral tests
findings.body: Both `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` and `Admin::EmbeddingController` specs only assert that the class is a subclass of `AdminController`. There are no tests for create/update/destroy (including the blank category falling back to uncategorized, validation error rendering, or non-existent id handling) or for the show/update serialization of the embedding endpoint. Basic request specs would have caught the nil-host 500 in the controllers and the no-op `update` action.
